tiles: The abundance and quiet tension of a Dutch still life
A small set of prints I ended up loving
challenge: What drew me to Jan Davidsz. de Heem wasn't only the fruit and foliage — it was the way Baroque still lifes hold abundance and tension in the same frame, with light that feels candlelit even when it isn't. I wanted to actually understand what the painters were doing, not just copy the look.
approach: I spent time reading about de Heem and the Dutch Golden Age, then drafted dozens of variations trying to capture that particular warmth, the deep shadow that lets a single grape catch the eye, and the way every object seems to lean into the arrangement. I kept the pieces that felt like they'd actually taught me something about how these paintings work.
result: The six images here are the ones that stuck with me — the ones where the mood of a Baroque still life came through and that I genuinely enjoyed looking at. I made them available as prints in case anyone else finds them as warm and satisfying to live with as I did.
